headline: US tech stocks lifted last night on strong AI optimism while the ASX slipped today, with oil's sharp 4% drop and a big NRL Grand Final win for the Roosters dominating the day's conversation.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS nudged up 1% today in a modest bounce — no specific catalyst in the news, but lithium stocks have been sensitive to any positive global demand signals. The stock remains deeply underwater overall (down ~57% on your cost base), so today's move is a small reprieve rather than a turning point.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOG rose almost 1% last night ahead of its Q3 earnings report. Deutsche Bank flagged strong expected Search revenue growth, and the broader NASDAQ rally helped lift it further. Wall Street is watching closely to see if AI-driven ad revenue can beat Q2's stumble.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT gained 0.84% last night with Morgan Stanley saying Q1 results should match expectations on the back of strong Azure (cloud computing) momentum. Earnings are due soon and sentiment is positive heading in.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE was the biggest ASX faller in your portfolio today, dropping about 1%. Emerging markets have been under pressure as the stronger Aussie dollar and global risk-off sentiment weighed. Nothing structural — just broader market jitters.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG dipped 0.54% today, dragged by the soft ASX session. As a broadly diversified fund, it tends to mirror the overall market. No specific news — just a quiet, slightly negative day on the ASX.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI slipped 0.54% today despite ongoing buzz around AI. The ASX-listed AI ETF can lag its US counterparts by a session since it tracks global AI companies priced overnight. The US NASDAQ's 1.1% gain last night should be a mild tailwind when the market reopens tomorrow.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS fell 0.47% today even though the US market it tracks was up last night — this is normal timing lag. VTS reflects last night's US prices when it opens on the ASX, so today's dip may simply be catch-up from an earlier session. The underlying US market is in good shape.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: DHHF edged down 0.43% today, in line with the modest ASX pullback. As a broadly diversified all-growth fund it tracks global markets across many regions — nothing company-specific to flag, just a soft day on the ASX.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO was essentially flat last night, dipping just 0.18%. GTA 6 remains the big catalyst to watch — reports say Rockstar rebuilt the game 'from the ground up' and Wall Street will be watching the November 19 earnings call closely for any updates on the release timeline.

watch_today.title: MSFT & GOOG earnings in focus — both reporting soon
watch_today.detail: Microsoft and Alphabet are both due to report Q1/Q3 earnings imminently (MSFT's Q1 and GOOG's Q3 are the next major catalysts). Morgan Stanley says MSFT should match expectations on Azure strength. Deutsche Bank is bullish on GOOG's Search revenue. Both stocks have been rising in anticipation — sit tight, these are the moments long-term holders are rewarded for patience.

watch_today.title: GOOG Q3 earnings — strong expectations, watch the result
watch_today.detail: Alphabet stock rose last night ahead of Q3 results. Deutsche Bank is flagging strong Search revenue growth, and analysts are watching whether AI-driven ad products are gaining real traction. You're up about 10.6% on your GOOG position — no reason to move before results, just watch what they report.

watch_today.title: PLS still deeply underwater — today's bounce is noise
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals gained 1% today, which sounds nice but you're still down about 57% on your original investment. There's no major lithium demand catalyst in today's news. Long-term lithium thesis remains intact (EV demand, energy transition) but the recovery timeline is uncertain. No reason to sell at this depth — hold and wait.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 is the only thing that matters here
watch_today.detail: Take-Two was flat last night. Reports say Rockstar rebuilt GTA 6 from the ground up, and the November 19 earnings call is shaping up as a huge catalyst. You're down about 5% on your TTWO position — the long-term thesis is entirely tied to GTA 6's eventual release. Hold through the noise.

watch_today.title: Oil fell sharply — watch what this means for inflation
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) dropped 4.2% last night to $99.34 a barrel. Cheaper oil is generally good for consumers (lower petrol prices) and could ease inflation pressures, which might give the RBA less reason to keep rates high. Keep an eye on how this feeds into the November RBA decision.

watch_today.title: RBA November meeting building — rate decision looms
watch_today.detail: CommBank economists are sticking with a November RBA rate decision call, though they say the outlook is uncertain. Some commentators are warning further rate rises could tip the economy toward recession. Watch for more economic data this week — any surprise figures could shift expectations quickly.

world.summary: The US midterms are dominating global political headlines, with Trump already laying the groundwork to dispute results. Meanwhile, the Iran-Israel conflict is escalating, oil has fallen sharply, and a major AI cost breakthrough was announced.

stories.title: Trump preparing to claim midterm results are 'rigged' before votes are even counted
stories.why_it_matters: Reports say Trump and his allies are already building a public narrative that the upcoming US midterm elections will be stolen or rigged — before a single vote is counted. This mirrors the playbook used after the 2020 presidential election and risks deepening political instability in the US regardless of results. For investors, prolonged US political uncertainty tends to create volatility in markets.

stories.title: DOJ charges 28 California residents with voting-related crimes amid Trump's voter fraud push
stories.why_it_matters: The US Department of Justice has charged 28 California residents — all green card holders (legal permanent residents, not citizens) — with illegally registering to vote or actually voting. Trump has made illegal voting by non-citizens a central political claim. Critics argue the DOJ is being weaponised for political purposes ahead of the midterms, while supporters say it vindicates concerns about election integrity. Either way, it's a significant escalation.

stories.title: US Defence Secretary Hegseth makes unannounced visit to Israel amid Iran war fears
stories.why_it_matters: US Defence Secretary Hegseth has made a surprise, unannounced trip to meet Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu as tensions over a potential wider war with Iran remain high. Iran's military commanders are publicly warning the 'world will be amazed' at their next moves, while Houthi forces in Yemen killed 58 people in an attack on a military camp. The Middle East conflict is far from over and any escalation could spike oil prices — which just had their biggest single-day drop in months.

stories.title: Oil crashes 4.2% — biggest daily drop in months
stories.why_it_matters: Crude oil (WTI) fell from $103.66 to $99.34 a barrel last night — a drop of 4.2% in a single session. This is significant because cheaper oil feeds into lower petrol prices for everyday Australians within weeks, and reduces one of the big inflation drivers that has been keeping interest rates high. The drop appears linked to easing immediate Middle East supply fears and broader demand concerns. Watch this closely — if it holds, it's good news for your hip pocket and for the RBA's rate decisions.

stories.title: Britain can't handle global crises without rejoining EU, says major thinktank
stories.why_it_matters: A prominent UK thinktank has published a report arguing that Britain is simply unable to respond effectively to major international crises — from the Russia-Ukraine war to the Iran conflict — without closer ties to the European Union. Brexit has left the UK diplomatically isolated at a time when coordinated Western responses matter most, the report argues. The finding is politically explosive in the UK and adds to pressure on the Labour government to reconsider post-Brexit arrangements.

politics.summary: The RBA's November meeting is shaping up as the dominant story in Australian economic life, with debate intensifying over whether another rate rise could tip the economy into recession.

stories.title: CommBank economists hold their November RBA rate call — but it's on a knife's edge
stories.why_it_matters: Commonwealth Bank's economists are maintaining their forecast that the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) will move on rates at its November meeting, but they're flagging significant uncertainty. The RBA has been lifting rates aggressively to fight inflation, and there's growing concern that too much tightening could push the economy into recession. For mortgage holders on variable rates, this is a week worth watching.

stories.title: Warning: further rate rises risk pushing economy 'over the edge'
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Morning Herald is reporting that economists are warning the RBA risks 'tipping the economy over the edge' if it continues raising rates. Australia's household debt levels are among the highest in the world, meaning rate rises bite harder here than in most countries. A recession would mean rising unemployment and falling consumer spending — which would hurt everything from retail stocks to property values.

stories.title: Independent Australia: RBA's 'extreme' rates already pushing toward recession
stories.why_it_matters: A more strident warning from Independent Australia, arguing the RBA's current interest rate settings are already at 'extreme' levels and are actively damaging the economy. The piece argues that waiting for inflation to fully come down before easing rates is a dangerous gamble. This reflects a real tension in Australian economic policy right now — inflation is still elevated, but growth is slowing fast.

ai.summary: The big AI labs are racing to release new models, a major data breach is threatening the industry's biggest names, and a new AI model has slashed costs by 70% overnight.

stories.title: Anthropic, Google and OpenAI all preparing new AI models simultaneously
stories.why_it_matters: The Information is reporting that all three of the world's leading AI companies — Anthropic (makers of Claude), Google (Gemini), and OpenAI (ChatGPT) — are simultaneously preparing major new model releases. This kind of simultaneous race means rapid improvements are coming for everyday users, but it also means the competitive landscape is fierce. For your GOOG and GXAI.AX holdings, an AI arms race keeps investment high but also keeps the competitive pressure intense.

stories.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash launches — cuts AI costs by 70%
stories.why_it_matters: A new AI model called MiniMax M3.1 Flash has launched, claiming to cut the cost of running AI tasks by 70% compared to existing models. This is a big deal — cheaper AI means more businesses can afford to use it, which accelerates adoption across every industry. It also puts pressure on OpenAI, Google and Anthropic to reduce their own prices. Lower AI costs are generally good for the broader economy, even if they compress margins for the big AI providers.

stories.title: OpenCode data breach could expose OpenAI, Anthropic and Google user data
stories.why_it_matters: A security breach at a platform called OpenCode may have exposed user data connected to accounts at OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google's AI services. The exact scale is unclear, but if confirmed it could affect millions of users of these AI tools. Trust and security are increasingly important for AI adoption — any major breach can slow enterprise uptake. Worth monitoring if you use any of these AI services yourself.

stories.title: Australia's online safety watchdog flags major gaps in AI regulation
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's eSafety Commissioner has flagged that current laws have significant gaps when it comes to regulating AI — particularly around harmful content, deepfakes, and AI-generated material targeting children. The watchdog is calling for new rules to be developed urgently. This signals that Australian AI regulation is coming, which could affect how AI tools are offered and used in this country — relevant for your GXAI.AX holding which tracks global AI companies.

stories.title: AI medical scribes face stricter oversight from Australia's TGA
stories.source: Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (RACGP)
stories.why_it_matters: The TGA (Therapeutic Goods Administration — Australia's medicine regulator) is moving to impose stricter oversight on AI tools used by doctors to automatically transcribe and summarise patient consultations. These 'medical scribes' are already widely used in GP clinics. The RACGP says greater scrutiny is needed to ensure patient safety and data privacy. This shows AI is moving fast enough in healthcare that regulators are scrambling to keep up.

sport.summary: The Rugby League World Cup has kicked off with its opening round, the NRL Grand Final saw the Roosters edge the Knights, and there's plenty of transfer and selection news ahead of the November internationals.

stories.title: Roosters beat Knights 19-18 in the NRL Grand Final
stories.why_it_matters: In a thriller at Accor Stadium on Sunday, the Sydney Roosters claimed the NRL premiership with a 19-18 victory over the Newcastle Knights. It was a one-point final — as tight as it gets. The result gives the Roosters their latest premiership and ends what was a remarkable Knights campaign to reach the decider.

stories.title: Rugby League World Cup: What we learned from the opening round
stories.why_it_matters: The Rugby League World Cup has officially kicked off and ESPN has published its key takeaways from the opening round of matches. No detailed article text is available, but the RLWC is always a massive event for league fans across Australia, New Zealand, and the Pacific.

stories.title: Four debutants loom in Kangaroos shake-up; Kiwis get big judiciary boost ahead of November 1
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's Kangaroos are set for a big shakeup for the November 1 RLWC match, with four potential debutants in the frame. Meanwhile the New Zealand Kiwis have received a significant boost from the judiciary — meaning a key player who was facing a ban has been cleared to play. The November 1 clash is shaping up as a genuine battle.

stories.title: Broncos lock in rising duo on new deals; PNG land key signing — NRL Daily
stories.why_it_matters: The Brisbane Broncos have secured two of their rising young players on new contracts — a positive sign for the club's future under coach Michael Maguire. Meanwhile, the PNG (Papua New Guinea) national team — who are making their RLWC debut — have signed a key figure to bolster their campaign. PNG's inclusion in the World Cup is a huge moment for rugby league's expansion in the Pacific.

markets.summary: The ASX slipped 0.33% today in a quiet session, while last night US markets were clearly in the green — the NASDAQ jumped 1.1% on AI and tech enthusiasm. The big standout was oil, which crashed 4.2% last night — the largest single-day drop in recent months. The Aussie dollar is sitting at exactly USD 0.70, up slightly.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Soft session today — nothing dramatic, just mild selling across the board.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session was positive — steady gains as US earnings optimism builds.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night's standout performer — tech and AI stocks led the charge, up over 1%.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Biggest story in markets — oil crashed 4.2% last night. Good news for petrol prices and inflation.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold barely moved — essentially flat. Still trading near historic highs.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar hit exactly USD 0.70 — a psychologically important level, up slightly on the day.
